group: insects: Morpho butterflies (Chazot et al. 2021 J Evol Biol: 911 specimens, 30 species on Morpho_MCC_tree.tre; forewing 22 LMs & hindwing 18 LMs)

data.landmarks: Chazot N, Blandin P, Debat V, Elias M, Condamine FL 2021 J Evol Biol 34:1076-1090; Zenodo 5391696 (`Chazotetal_2021_forewing_ProcCoord.txt` 22 2D landmarks, `Chazotetal_2021_hindwing_ProcCoord.txt` 18 2D landmarks across 911 specimens and 30 Morpho species).
data.phylogeny: Time-calibrated MCC phylogeny `Chazotetal_2021_Morpho_MCC_tree.tre` (30 matched Morpho species, crown age ~28 Myr).

what_thompson_specifically_adds: Tests the portfolio's Papilionoidea / butterfly entry on true 2D wing landmarks across both forewings and hindwings on a time-calibrated tree, allowing a direct comparison of Lepidoptera wing venation/outline against Hymenoptera (hornets, bees) and Diptera (Drosophila).

hypotheses.statement: Across the 30 Morpho species means, Thompson-7 captures > 45% of between-species Procrustes variance on both forewings (22 LMs) and hindwings (18 LMs).
hypotheses.reasoning: Butterfly wing landmarks include margin/apex/tornus contour points alongside discal cell veins, giving a slightly higher global coordinate share than Hymenoptera interior venation (38.8-42.2%).

hypotheses.statement: Phylogenetic signal on `Morpho_MCC_tree.tre`: Pagel's lambda > 0.5 (best model != White Noise) in both forewing and hindwing shape spaces.
hypotheses.reasoning: Canopy vs understory flight-strata syndromes in Morpho follow well-known subgeneric clades on the calibrated MCC tree.

hypotheses.statement: Leave-one-species-out phylogenetic prediction on `Morpho_MCC_tree.tre` beats the grand consensus (median Procrustes RMS ratio < 0.90, paired one-sided Wilcoxon p < 0.01) on forewing shape.
hypotheses.reasoning: Matches the 0.85 subjective prior registered for butterflies in `thompson_dataset_portfolio.json`.

hypotheses.statement: Sexual dimorphism vs interspecific divergence: within-species male -> female wing shape vectors have a higher Thompson-7 variance share than between-species divergence on the forewing.
hypotheses.reasoning: Like ant caste polyphenism, sexual wing-shape dimorphism in Morpho (broader female wings for egg load vs narrower male patrol wings) is an ontogenetic scaling of the same wing imaginal disc.
